title: Attention shape fuzzing + differential regression harness for v2->v3 kernel transitions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Upgrading kernels from FlashAttention v2 to v3 introduces nontrivial codepaths that change micro-tiling, memory layout, and precision fallback behavior. We have observed intermittent latency spikes and rare correctness deltas for long-tail attention shapes under mixed tenant workloads. Goal: Build a reproducible, automated harness that (1) fuzzes attention input shapes and sequence distributions, (2) runs paired v2 vs v3 kernel comparisons under controlled concurrency and memory pressure, (3) produces differential telemetry (latency/quality deltas) and ranked candidate regressions for engineering review. This ticket focuses on the harness, metrics, and an initial policy for automated rollback gates. We will not change kernel implementations here—only detection and triage automation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI job that executes 10k weighted shape samples per day with both v2 and v3 kernels and posts a summary artifact to the stability dashboard.
2) Differential report shows per-shape: median latency delta, p95 delta, correctness checksum mismatch rate, and kernel-oscillation count.
3) Alert rule configured: if any shape cohort shows p95 latency regression >25ms with >1% freq OR checksum mismatches >0.01%, create ENG ticket and attach diagnostics.
4) Harness integrates with runtime PR process (GitHub action) and blocks canary rollout when alerts trip.
5) Documentation + runbook added to Confluence with triage steps and reproducer collection commands.
out_of_scope:
1) Kernel bug fixes or perf tuning work (will be separate tickets).
2) End-to-end customer-facing rollback automation across Dedicated clusters (future work).
3) Long-term ML-based anomaly detection—this is rule-driven initially.
plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket): implement shape sampler + differential runner + minimal telemetry extraction (latency histograms, KV cache pressure, CUDA OOM indicators, decode jitter). Phase 2: integrate with daily CI and stability dashboard, add auto-ticketing and lightweight grouping heuristics. Phase 3 (follow-ups): candidate prioritization by customer impact and synthetic replay harness. Implementation steps:
- Build shape-fuzzer module that produces a corpus of weighted shapes (batch_size, seq_len, num_heads, head_dim, layer_idx distribution).
- Implement differential runner that executes same inputs on v2 and v3 kernels in an isolated worker with deterministic seeding.
- Capture metrics: per-invocation timings (start→end, kernel selection path), memory working set, kernel switch count, checksum of final logits/next-token probabilities.
- Produce artifact JSON summarized by cohort and push to S3.
- Wire CI job + dashboard ingestion + alert rules.
- Add docs and runbook.
Estimated effort: 5 points, cross-functional review with Applied ML and Observability.
